messages:
maria: Quick follow-up to the onboarding RFC — need a concrete plan for runtime compatibility checks before admitting models to hosted + dedicated. Main question: which gates are automated vs manual override?

alex: My proposal: automated gates = correctness (eval prompts), perf benchmarks (p50/p95 under target batch sizes), memory footprint, quantization smoke test, and ops/kernel compatibility. Manual: unusual architectures, custom ops that require vendor sign-off.

samir: +1. Also add a kernel-compat check: ensure model can run with our optimized kernels or that fallback path is acceptable w/o huge latency hit. And KV-cache layout test for chat models (off-by-one bugs crop up).

jia: What numeric thresholds are we enforcing? For hosted we should be stricter. Suggest: perf thresholds by family — p95 <= 2x baseline for small models, <=1.5x for medium, p50 within 1.2x. Cost-per-token delta < 30%. Eval regression tolerance: NLL/EM within 3% relative.

kevin: Those are decent starting points but we should tie to per-family baselines. For cost-per-token use the microbench harness. Example command we can standardize in CI:```bench-run --model {MODEL} --profile tokens=1000 --batch=8 --warmup=100 --record=perf.json```This will produce p50/p95 and token/sec.

infra-bot: CI job created: eng-ml/model-onboard-bench. Runs perf, mem, ops-compat, quant smoke. Artifacts stored at s3://redwood-onboard-artifacts/1801234567/ (job id).

maria: For ops-compat: how do we detect custom CUDA ops or .so dependencies? Can we auto-reject or just flag?

samir: We can run an artifact inspection step (ldd-like). If nonstandard shared objects are present, mark the model as "manual review required". Also run a sandbox container that loads the model to capture missing kernels at runtime.

jia: Also we need deterministic eval harness: seed RNGs, run canonical prompt set, and store outputs as golden artifacts so regression checks are reproducible.

alex: Decision draft: automated gates = (1) signature match (inputs/outputs + types), (2) ops/kernel compat OK or documented fallback, (3) perf within family-specific thresholds, (4) memory footprint < node capacity minus headroom, (5) eval metrics within regression window. Any failure -> prebake/triage queue. On-call/eng-ml can approve overrides with documented reason.

maria: Flow idea: PR to model-registry triggers CI bench job, posts artifacts + dashboard link to #model-onboard-notifications, creates triage task if any gate fails. Owners: eng-ml for triage and eval failures, eng-runtime for kernel/op issues.

kevin: Can we add an automated quantization check? Quick flow: run 8-bit and 4-bit conversions and compare eval deltas. Prototype script:```quant-check --model {MODEL} --modes q8,q4 --tolerance 2.5 --out results.json```If delta > tolerance -> flag. I'll add this to the bench job.

samir: Also we should capture KV-cache memory growth for conversation lengths and run a long-tail eviction test (simulate 1000-step session). Catchs subtle memory leaks or cache mis-indexing.

jia: Add embedding regressions too (cosine similarity thresholds) for retrieval use-cases. And include a small set of seeded queries per domain.

alex: On rollouts: admitted models should start with a controlled canary (5% traffic cap) and monitors on latency, error rate, and quality (regression on sampled prompts). Console must expose per-version metrics and allow automatic rollback.

maria: I'll draft a formal checklist and update the RFC with these gates + flow. Action items: maria write checklist by EOD Wed; alex implement family-baseline flag in bench harness; kevin add quant script and hook into CI; samir add ops-detection + sandbox run; jia add deterministic eval artifacts and embedding checks. I'll create the triage label in the registry and wire the notification channel.

alex: :thumbsup: I'll start a branch for the harness changes.

kevin: :eyes: on the quant script, ping me if you need sample models or perf traces.

infra-bot: Reminder: eng-ml/model-onboard-bench scheduled nightly for queued PRs. Please ensure artifacts are uploaded within 1 hour of job completion.

maria: Thanks everyone — I'll post the checklist draft when ready.
